text.p: The Bangladesh parliament has endorsed the country's budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year beginning on Tuesday, passing an appropriation bill amid an opposition walk-out late on Monday.
Before placing the appropriation bill, Finance Minister S.A.M.S.Kibria reduced tariff rates on several items he proposed in his budget speech on June 12.
He withdrew the proposed 2.5 percent import duty on some drugs and their raw materials and allowed their duty-free import.
Kibria also exempted a 2.5 percent duty on imports of raw cotton and reduced duties on textile machinery to 2.5 percent from 7.5 percent for a period up to December 31, 1999.

He retained the 7.5 percent customs duty on imports of scrap ships instead of the 15 percent rate he had proposed in the budget. A proposal to impose a 2.5 percent import duty on diesel engines has also been withdrawn.

Finance ministry officials on Tuesday said the duty cut might cost one billion taka in revenue losses. "The government will strive to tide over the loss by expanding (the) tax net and raising administrative efficiency," one official said.
The 1997/98 budget projects expenditure at 277.86 billion taka against revenue of 196.24 billion taka, leaving a deficit of 81.62 billion taka.
Former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia led the legislators of her main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) out of parliament, in protest at some of the budget measures.
"We are staging this walk-out to protest the anti-development budget that levied taxes on the people," Khaleda said.
